PullRequest.Title: connectors: make unknown connector status actionable instead of "Checking…" forever
PullRequest.Body:
## Problem

If the GitHub session that carries `write:plugin_gateway_connections` goes away, VS Code falls back to the unscoped connector catalog, where every connection status is `unknown`. This happens on sign out + sign in, when the token is revoked or expires, or when the catalog request fails.

- **Browse:** every connector this account connected on this machine shows **"Checking connection"** with a disabled **"Checking…"** button. It never resolves: connector scopes are only requested after an explicit user action, and the only action is disabled.
- **MCP Servers:** the connector MCP servers disappear without any explanation.

The cause is in `reconcileRecord()`. It mapped "status cannot be known without user action" to `checking`, and the UI treats that state as busy everywhere.

## Fix

- **New `unverified` install state** for recorded connectors whose status is `unknown` or not yet known. `checking` is now only reported while a check is actually in flight.
  - This is a separate state rather than more special cases in `checking`, because `checking` is shared with plugin and MCP records and every consumer treats it as busy.
- **New `ICustomizationMarketplaceInstallService.checkConnectorConnections()`**, which wraps `ICopilotConnectorsService.checkConnection()` (authorize, then refresh).
  - It runs once for the whole account: the catalog refresh resolves every recorded connector at once, and concurrent calls join the same operation.
  - It never connects or disconnects anything, so it stays separate from `repair()`, which reconnects.
- **Browse rows, cards and the marketplace detail** show **"Connection status not checked"** with an enabled **Check Connection** action. **Disconnect** stays available. A failed check stays actionable and shows the error in a hover and an alert.
- **MCP Servers** shows a notice naming the connectors whose MCP servers are hidden ("MCP servers from Copilot connectors (Mail, Acme Notes) are hidden until their connection status is checked."), with a **Check Connection** action.
- **Shared wording:** labels come from `connectorPresentation.ts` (a new `'check'` action label), so Browse, the detail page and MCP Servers use the same text.
- **No automatic scope requests:** connector OAuth scopes are still only requested after the user clicks.

## Related bugs

- **Unknown status shows "Connect":** partly addressed. Connectors with a local record on this machine now show Check Connection. Connectors without a record still show "Connect" while the catalog is unscoped; that is left for a follow-up.
- **Stale "Disconnected" records:** not changed by this PR.

## How to test

1. Connect a connector.
2. Sign out of the GitHub session that has the connector scope, then sign back in. In the connector test bed you can instead run **Connector Test Bed: Revoke Connector Scope**.
3. Open **Chat Customizations → Browse → `@type:mcp`**. The connector shows "Connection status not checked" with an enabled **Check Connection**.
4. Open **MCP Servers**. A notice explains which connector servers are hidden.
5. Click **Check Connection**. The authorization prompt appears, then the connector resolves to Connected and its MCP servers reappear.

## Validation

- New tests:
  - Install service: losing the scope gives `unverified`; the check runs once, shows `checking` while in flight, then resolves to `installed`; a failed check stays actionable.
  - Discovery page: row label and button states.
  - Connectors service: no consent prompt after scope loss until an explicit check.
  - MCP list: notice text and button states.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` on the connector-related aiCustomization suites (install service, discovery page, connectors service, MCP list, presentation, workbench service, marketplace provider): **378 passing**.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/**/*.test.js"`: **769 passing**.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: no errors in changed code. It does report errors in `platform/agentHost` because the local `@github/copilot-sdk` in `node_modules` is out of date.
- `npm run eslint` on the changed files: clean. The pre-commit hygiene check passes.
- I did not run the end-to-end flow above in the test bed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added bulk call, per-record synchronous emissions, immediate observable delivery, and full-tree render path are directly traced in repository code. Only the exact frame-time cost and typical connector/MCP counts are uncertain; the multiplicative mechanism and trigger are not.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and DOM/tree nodes rebuilt by MCP and marketplace views
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N recorded connectors and M visible MCP/tree entries, the account-wide check produces up to N independent install-service events, each triggering O(M) filtering and tree reconstruction, for O(N×M) synchronous UI work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated full-list reconstruction increases completion latency and can cause dropped frames when checking an account with several recorded connectors and a sizable MCP list.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no account-wide explicit check that transitioned all unknown connector records together, so this bulk unverified-to-resolved path and its per-record UI notification burst did not exist.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new check reconciles all applicable connector records after one catalog refresh; reconcileRecords runs reconcileRecord for every record, and each changed record immediately calls emitChange rather than publishing the completed batch once.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1009 newly invokes `await this.reconcileRecords(this.getApplicableConnectorRecords())` for the account-wide check, creating the collection-wide state transition whose existing per-record `emitChange()` behavior fans out into repeated full UI renders.
Findings.Title: Batch connector reconciliation before notifying the UI
Findings.Impact: Clicking Check Connection with multiple recorded connectors can rebuild the entire MCP list once per connector before the action completes. This is especially visible in profiles with several connectors and dozens or more local, runtime, gallery, plugin, and provider MCP entries.
Findings.Evidence: The added await at line 1009 passes every applicable connector record to reconcileRecords. reconcileRecords maps them to reconcileRecord, whose connector branch is synchronous and whose changed-state branch calls emitChange once per record (lines 507-556). emitChange invalidates the snapshot and fires an Emitter; McpListWidget observes that event in an autorun and calls filterServers (lines 2139-2142), which reconstructs all server matchers/entries and calls renderMcpTree, including two list.setChildren calls (lines 2967-3068). Observable event delivery uses a separate synchronous transaction for each fire, so these renders are not coalesced.
Findings.Recommendation: Reconcile the connector records while suppressing per-record notifications, then invalidate the snapshot and emit one change after the batch is complete (including a single final notification on failure/cancellation as needed). Preserve the existing start/end checking notifications and avoid exposing partial per-connector completion states.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render recorded connectors after connector authorization/catalog status becomes unknown in Browse, marketplace detail, and MCP Servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Connector/account change reconciliation computes `unverified`, invalidates the installation snapshot, and synchronously updates visible connector controls and the MCP notice. No new external operation must complete merely to display the state.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of recorded connectors for the active account; the MCP view also scans the complete installation snapshot and its existing MCP collections.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reconciliation is launched for applicable records with Promise.all, but connector-state computation is synchronous. Each changed record can notify observers independently; there is no event coalescing across the collection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The installation snapshot is cached until `emitChange`; each emission invalidates and reconstructs it. This state-display path does not perform a catalog fetch or request authorization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the state computation, snapshot invalidation, observable notification, and UI consumers are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical connector counts are not encoded in the repository, but plural-connector behavior is explicitly supported and tested.
Scenarios.Verdict: The unverified-state presentation itself is inexpensive and removes a perpetual busy state; no separate regression was reported for merely rendering the notice.

Scenarios.Scenario: Check connector connections from Browse, marketplace detail, MCP Servers, or before running an unverified connector customization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action awaits connector authorization, a forced catalog refresh, an optional Agent Host connector-session refresh when connected membership changes, then reconciliation of every applicable connector record. All are on the action completion path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read authentication sessions and, when connector scope is absent, request creation of a scoped session/consent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One joined authorization operation per account-wide check; session creation occurs only when no suitable scoped session exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No explicit recovery action reached connector authorization from an unknown recorded-installation state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Authorization or user consent must complete before the catalog query can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one connector catalog query using the authorized session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one forced catalog query for the globally coalesced check, independent of connector count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The unverified-record workflow had no user-triggered authoritative refresh; ordinary connector discovery could still issue its existing cached/unscoped query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response is required before connector states can be reconciled and the action completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh live Agent Host connector sessions when authoritative connected membership changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero or one call per catalog refresh, not per connector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This existing refresh was reached by other connector catalog updates, but the PR introduces this explicit recovery path to it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When membership changes, this awaited refresh delays completion of the catalog refresh and therefore the check action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One account-wide request resolves N recorded connectors; subsequent UI work scales with N records and M MCP/list entries. Effective boundary cardinality remains one account operation after coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `pendingConnectorCheck` globally coalesces concurrent calls from all surfaces. Connector authorization also joins `authorizationPromise`. Record reconciliation fans out with Promise.all, but its connector branch is synchronous and emits independently per resolved record.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm scoped authentication session avoids `createSession`; a cold/missing scope invokes session creation. The explicit check intentionally calls `refresh` directly, so it always performs a fresh catalog query rather than using the normal refresh-interval cache. Concurrent checks share the same promise; failures are not negatively cached and a later explicit retry runs again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: global coalescing and boundary cardinalities are explicit, while the added bulk reconcile is directly connected to synchronous per-record UI emissions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network/auth latency and typical N/M values vary by account and profile; this affects severity, not the proven repeated-render mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: One medium finding was reported because the single account-wide check publishes N record transitions separately, synchronously rebuilding the full MCP tree and other visible views for each record. The external boundaries themselves are properly account-wide and coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disconnect an unverified recorded connector from Browse or marketplace detail
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The explicit Disconnect action awaits connector authorization, one disconnect request, and catalog polling until the connector is no longer connected or the existing timeout expires; the local record is then removed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read sessions and optionally create a connector-scoped authentication session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One joined authorization operation for the selected connector action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The service/UI guards did not allow Disconnect from the newly distinguished unknown state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before disconnect can be sent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one disconnect command and poll the connector catalog until disconnected or timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One disconnect request plus time-bounded catalog queries for one selected connector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bounded disconnect protocol existed for installed/missing/error connectors, but was not reachable from the formerly busy unknown-state UI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The record is not removed and the UI operation does not complete until remote disconnection is observed or fails.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user-selected connector. Poll count scales with remote completion time up to the existing timeout, not with the number of recorded connectors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Duplicate uninstalls for the same connector key join `pendingUninstalls`; different connector keys are not globally limited, but the reviewed UI gesture starts one operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm scoped session avoids new consent. Disconnect polling intentionally refreshes authoritative state; no new cache is introduced or defeated beyond exposing the existing operation for `unverified`.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: state guards, same-key promise coalescing, and the disconnect polling loop are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote propagation controls poll count and duration, but the operation remains single-connector and timeout-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance issue: the new reachability is intentional, user-triggered, same-key coalesced, and reuses a bounded single-connector protocol.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. Traced the new connector check and disconnect workflows through authentication, network, Agent Host IPC, reconciliation, snapshot caching, observer delivery, and visible Browse/detail/MCP rendering. Submitted one medium repeated-render finding; no regression-fix learning signal was warranted because the prior perpetual busy state was correctness/UX rather than a concrete performance mechanism.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
